surface_mechanism_description: The reaction mechanism involves the chemisorption of Me3AuPMe3 molecules on a gold surface, where CH3 and PMe3 ligands remain on the surface, causing self-limiting adsorption. The H2 plasma removes these ligands as CH4 and possibly (tri,di)methylphosphine/phosphine groups, allowing new precursor molecules to adsorb. At higher temperatures, the stability of the ligands decreases, leading to precursor decomposition. The decomposition is linked to the desorption of CH3 ligands forming CH4 and the removal of PMe3 ligands, which are less stable at higher temperatures. On SiO2 surfaces, the nucleation occurs on Si-OH groups.
evidence: The reaction mechanism was investigated using in-situ RAIRS and in-vacuo XPS measurements, which confirmed that the CH3 and PMe3 ligands remain on the gold surface after chemisorption. The H2 plasma removes these ligands as CH4 and possibly (tri,di)methylphosphine/phosphine groups. The decomposition behavior of the Me3AuPMe3 precursor on a gold surface is linked to the stability of the ligands, with PMe3 ligands being less stable at higher temperatures. The nucleation on SiO2 surfaces occurs on Si-OH groups.
